title: Decouple subnet provisioner into plugin lifecycle and introduce provider matrix for safe cloud SDK upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The existing subnet provisioning code is a monolithic terraform module that mixes long-lived networking resources, ephemeral zone-level helpers, and provider-specific hacks. This has caused frequent plan churn, slow applies across workspaces, and fragile provider upgrades (we've seen subtle AWS provider behavior changes in past upgrades).

Goal: Split the subnet provisioner into two orthogonal pieces: (1) a stable core 'network-contract' module that exposes explicit interfaces for VPC/subnet/route table lifecycle and (2) a plugin-oriented 'subnet-provisioner' lifecycle module for zone/ephemeral resources (EIPs, NAT assignment shims, AZ helpers). Introduce a provider-matrix pattern so each workspace can opt into pinned provider version sets (aws/gcp/az) while allowing a migration rollout to newer SDKs without mass simultaneous plan churn.

Success criteria: reduced plan churn for networking changes in >90% of infra workspaces, provider upgrades performed via opt-in workspace matrix with no service-impacting diffs, and overall terraform apply latency reduced by ~25% for networking stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Core network-contract module has stable API (inputs/outputs) and unit tests validating idempotency
Plugin-oriented subnet-provisioner supports registering provider aliases and can be toggled per-workspace
Migration script to transition legacy workspaces to provider-matrix with automated state moves and a rollback path
CI gating: terraform plan noise benchmark added and must show <=10% additional diffs during upgrade canary
At least three non-production workspaces migrated and validated with zero service incidents
updates: 2025-01-22 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem review flagged network plan churn as a recurring cost driver. Proposed split approach documented in design doc.

2025-01-28 - Jonah Kim: Spike complete. Validated that separating provider-specific resources into a provider_alias module removes provider version coupling across subnets. Prototype terraform modules in /modules/network-contract and /modules/subnet-plugin. Found edge case with route-table association ordering.

2025-02-02 - Infrastructure SIG: Decided to keep backward-compatible outputs on network-contract for 2 releases to allow gradual workspace migration. Trade-off: slight duplication in early rollout but reduces blast radius.
2025-02-06 - Claire Novak (PM): Requested that migration tooling include a dry-run mode and clear rollback instructions; prioritized for canary workspaces.

2025-02-10 - Jonah Kim: Opened PR #1284 with module split and a helper script that uses terraform state mv to move subnet resources into new module paths. Marked WIP until we validate plan noise on staging-1 and staging-2 workspaces.
2025-02-12 - Infra SRE (code review): Flagged provider matrix config needs explicit provider alias mapping for cross-account peering. Added acceptance test to ensure peering lifecycle intact.

2025-02-14 - Jonah Kim: Completed canary migration for staging-1. Plan diffs reduced by ~38% vs baseline and apply time was 22% faster. No incidents. Preparing runbook for broader rollouts. Moving ticket from In Progress -> In Review for module API approval.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: State migration can cause drift if not carefully ordered. Mitigation: migration script includes --targeted plan checkpoints and automated state backups; manual approval gate in CI.

Risk: Provider-specific behaviors (eg. AZ-level EIP allocation race) may surface under the new lifecycle. Mitigation: include provider shim tests and keep plugin toggles to disable new behavior per-workspace.
Risk: Teams may opt out and create forked module usages causing divergence. Mitigation: communicate migration schedule, provide automated codemod, and offer limited grace period with support.
